problem: Scale representation learning across robots with incompatible observation/action dimensions while transferring useful visual and proprioceptive knowledge.
contribution: Heterogeneous Pre-trained Transformers split policies into embodiment-specific stems/heads and a shared transformer trunk, supporting heterogeneous supervised pretraining and adaptation.
algorithm: Map vision/proprioception to fixed query tokens, process them with a shared trunk and regress normalized actions with Huber loss through task heads. Pretrain sampled embodiment stems/heads plus trunk; for new embodiments reinitialize stem/head and freeze the pretrained trunk.
observations: Vision and available measured proprioception. Default frozen ResNet18 features from one view; force/3D/tactile modalities are architectural possibilities, not all validated in the same experiment.
actions: Embodiment-specific normalized control outputs; source real tasks use relative or absolute pose actions at10Hz. Human video experiments use pose/2D surrogates rather than actual robot action labels.
embodiment_and_data: Default27datasets with maximum1000trajectories each and16Ktotal; scaling studies reach52datasets and1Bparameters. Real pet-care/assembly tasks use roughly100demos each across two embodiments.
experiments: Pretraining validation losses and separate downstream success tests; four simulation benchmarks and four real tasks. Real prose specifies15trials/task, while Figure12 caption says45trials/approach; Table3's exact aggregation/seed convention requires appendix confirmation.
baselines: From-scratch/no-trunk, no-proprioception and pretrained visual R3M, Voltron, VC-1; different pretraining/input access must remain explicit. Some simulator baselines use published source scores.

quantitative_result.value: Sweep Leftover Table3 HPT-B70.0±3.0%,HPT-XL76.7±3.3%,fromscratch43.3±3.8%,VC-153.3±2.6%. These are one task's source results, not a four-task average; exact Table3 uncertainty/denominator was not resolved by examined main text.
quantitative_result.location: PDF p10 Table3, p9 Section5.2 protocol

limitations: Dataset curation/filtering and pretraining objectives remain underexplored; heterogeneous training can converge slowly. Evaluations are short-horizon and typically below90%reliability. Missing proprioception can make simulator transfer unsuitable without finetuning.
code_and_license: Paper releases code/weights; this review did not inspect source/license files or execute HPT. Human-data surrogates require their own provenance.
hardware_adaptation: A useful alternative to a universal joint-action vector: keep embodiment-specific stems/heads and explicit measured-state availability. Frozen backbones still occupy memory; no NX fit/performance claim follows from only2%trainable parameters.
